Thanks for the call earlier. Per our internal product ops and procurement folks, we need a concise sizing worksheet that ties the reserved capacity commitment to an explicit SLA curve. In particular:

- Our peak is mid-day PST, sustained 1.2k reqs/min across a 3-hour window, with p99 latency goal of 180ms for short chat prompts (~512 tokens).

I've attached a quick CSV export of our telemetry (summitai-traffic-sample.csv). Can you confirm whether you would treat the overnight summarization as burstable versus part of committed capacity? Alex —

Thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. Quick answers up front:

- Overnight summarization can be treated as scheduled capacity and carved out of your committed pool (preferred for predictability) or priced as burst consumption if you need more headroom short-term. We usually recommend folding predictable nightly batch into the committed baseline with time-based sharding to avoid interfering with peak-day latency SLOs.
- On KV-cache: a 40% reuse rate materially reduces per-token cost for conversational flows; our sizer will apply a conservative cache hit assumption of 30% in the baseline and show an alternate scenario at 45% hit rate so you can see the delta.

I'll pull together a quick SLA-driven commitment sketch and a stressor profile mapping to show how many reserved GPUs we'd recommend under different p99 targets and growth curves. Looping in Karthik for the technical breakdown on token-econ and batching assumptions.

Ben

Alex / Ben —

I ran a quick back-of-envelope using the telemetry shape you sent. Summary of the stressor-profile assumptions I used (will put into the spreadsheet):

- Baseline prompt mix: 72% short chat (median 120 tokens input / 80 tokens output), 20% medium Q&A (300/250), 8% long-form summarization (input 1.8k / output 1.0k).
- Tokenization & batching: average model step cost assumes 32-token decoder chunking for longer responses; effective batching window 6ms during peak; concurrency target to keep p99 <= 180ms is ~140 live sessions per GPU for the short-chat profile on A100-like backends (quantized runtime).
- Night batch: scheduling window 02:00–06:00 PST; if folded into committed pool using time-based eviction we estimate it consumes the equivalent of ~2.5 sustained GPUs across the 4-hour window; as burst it would be ~0.7 GPUs of average additional load but with high variance at job start.
- Cache: using conservative 30% KV reuse reduces token execution by ~18% across the short-chat mix.

I'll attach a two-scenario table: 'Conservative commit' (assume 30% cache, 10% growth) and 'Aggressive commit' (45% cache, 30% growth). Also include a 'fallback routing' plan: evening batch -> reserved pool; spikes -> burst pool with pre-emptible instances.
